text:
Dear Dr. Sterling,

Thank you for evaluating this male patient, whom I am referring for an expert opinion. His cutaneous problems began during early childhood and have proven increasingly refractory over the years.

Recent tissue biopsies from his lower extremities confirmed a deep dermatophyte infection, characterized by invasive fungal elements extending into the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissues with associated suppurative granulomatous changes. Despite this severe fungal invasion, he has never developed fungal meningitis, and he has remained entirely free of any meningeal or neurological symptoms. Furthermore, he has no history of recurrent oral thrush, and his mucosal surfaces appear healthy.

We have carried out an initial immunological assessment. His total leukocyte count was entirely normal. Quantitative circulating immunoglobulin concentrations fell well within standard reference intervals. Lymphocyte phenotyping revealed a normal CD4+ T-cell subset proportion, and his total CD8+ T-cell count was also completely normal.

On general physical examination, his vital signs are stable, and cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal examinations are unremarkable. He works in office administration, does not smoke, and reports a non-contributory family history with no relatives affected by chronic skin conditions. His only current medications are over-the-counter loratadine and occasional acetaminophen.

Given the persistence and invasive nature of his presentation since his youth, I would greatly appreciate your assessment and recommendations regarding his ongoing management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Vance
